identity: ieo Windows WebView2 PDF-reader preview 0.1.2-preview.20261022 (installer PE version 0.0.0.0)
reason: The complete installer and reader paths implement a consented PDF reader and optional Google Drive reading-history synchronization. No malicious execution, credential theft, unauthorized transfer, or covert persistence was identified. Published bytes and bundled dependencies corroborate the claimed purpose.
methods: atomscan baseline and final JSON plus terminal scan
cleave facts including text/UTF-16 and matchable structural data
dnfile/dncil full installer and native-reader IL disassembly with metadata-token resolution; entry points, handlers, callbacks and async state machines traced
Safe extraction of CLR resources and ZIP without executing the program
forager retrieval retaining .forage.json provenance; package content and hash comparison
PE Authenticode structure and digest inspection using pefile and osslsigncode
static_execution_trace: Installer entry token 0x06000007: validates optional QA GUID, restricts installation to current-user LocalApplicationData/Programs, checks for an already-running reader, and presents install/remove confirmation outside explicit QA mode.

Installer Resource/Hash/Child and Main: reads ZIP/manifest resources, validates archive SHA-256 and all member sizes/hashes, rejects traversal/duplicate/oversized entries, stages a versioned release and creates desktop/Start-menu shortcuts and current-user uninstall registration. No fetched payload or automatic launch is present.

Installer updates an existing matching Run registration only; uninstall removes its own shortcuts/Run/uninstall entries and preserves reading data and program versions. Native StartupRegistration.Set is reached through the settings dispatcher; enabling login startup is a user setting.

Native reader creates a WinForms tray and WebView2 window. https://ieo.example/ is a local resource origin intercepted by Resource, not a remote C2 server. Resources are restricted to the local dist directory with traversal checks; Google APIs are the only permitted remote WebView request host.

Native GoogleAuth.Browser binds an ephemeral IPv4 loopback listener, opens Google OAuth in the default browser, generates state plus S256 PKCE, validates callback host/path/state, exchanges the authorization code at oauth2.googleapis.com, and requests drive.file and drive.appdata scopes.

GoogleAuth refresh/identify use the configured Google endpoints; Vault protects its own refresh grant, settings and imported migration snapshot with CurrentUser DPAPI. The installed-app OAuth client configuration is bundled publicly, not harvested from another application.

Reader Message validates both document origins and a finite method/argument schema. It provides settings, OAuth, file picking and cancellation, with QA window controls gated by QA mode. There is no general shell/command-execution RPC.
QA-only named pipe uses a current-user ACL and dispatches metrics/show/hide operations; QA remote debugging requires an explicit port option and binds to loopback.

Frontend imports chosen PDFs, renders PDF.js, stores library/progress in IndexedDB, exports backups, and writes reading-history JSON sidecars to the consenting user's Google Drive appDataFolder. Migration verifies copied records, rotates the writer identity, and retains historical data.

Dynamic script execution is WebView2 local bridge/migration initialization and the upstream PDF.js sandbox, not PowerShell. The Duplex literal is a PDF printer preference. High entropy and incidental opcode bytes lie primarily in compressed resource data, not an analysis-evasion execution path.

external_reference_checks.publisher_content: Fetched pages describe the same unsigned preview, PDF reading, Google Drive synchronization and tester-only authorization. Treated as corroborating claims, not proof of intent.
external_reference_checks.google_api_script: https://apis.google.com/js/api.js retrieved (14576 bytes); response inspected. It is in an inactive browser fallback when the native bridge exists.
external_reference_checks.google_identity_script: https://accounts.google.com/gsi/client retrieval attempted using forager; HTTP 403. Native bridge bypasses this fallback and implements OAuth itself.
external_reference_checks.google_endpoints: Native HTTP paths are fixed Google token/about endpoints; frontend authenticated operations are confined to Google Drive. Scope URLs and api.js were also followed by the archive scanner.

source_label_explanation: Exact submission/deployment circumstances are unknown. Plausible false-positive drivers are the unsigned, newly built custom .NET self-extractor, very high entropy from its ZIP resource, sparse PE imports, generic version metadata, and dual-use registry/DPAPI/script APIs. The supplied vendor names are predominantly generic/ML labels. These observations cannot establish why the source collected it or prove hostile intent.
rule_review: Relocated three managed process-module observations from selfpath to query; preserved matcher/scope/severity and updated the Defender/Malwarebytes exclusion consumer. Actual installer uses MainModule on another process.

Tightened PowerShell AddScript to a complete word; native WebView2 methods with longer names do not establish PowerShell. Added the separate WebView2 document-created-script observation. Empire agent and extracted inline MSBuild AddScript paths retain their findings.

Retained lowercase connect text as neutral vocabulary and required Winsock DLL context for the socket-name composite. Native reader connect is its OAuth RPC verb. Existing connect imports/ordinals and all other socket matchers are unchanged. The neutral token retains the original app/library/tool and Go-runtime exclusions, preserving the original matcher scope; a does-nothing Go fixture exposed this requirement during validation.
Relocated the unchanged WebView2Loader.dll matcher from masquerade to library-path references and updated its trojanized-sample consumer, preserving its effective scope/severity.
Relocated the unchanged BrotliDecode matcher from D2 identity to Brotli decompression; retained the D2 exception's path-plus-decoder requirements.

Relocated the unchanged Duplex literal matcher to source-literal metadata. Retired the unreferenced has-stream OR composite, whose Duplex branch did not establish Node.js. The canonical metadata/import/builtin::stream-require-reference detector remains unchanged.

Exact and ancestor consumers audited; no parent references to the moved process-info or WebView2 masquerade leaf. Broad library/tool exclusions were inspected via corpus diffs; PDF.js retains its accurate library identity. No supported attack finding was removed or lowered.
